niche: connected TV and streaming advertising agency
prompt_text: What is the best connected TV advertising agency?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” connected TV (CTV) advertising agency — the right partner depends on your goals (brand awareness vs performance), budget, target markets, creative needs, and whether you want programmatic buying, premium publisher packages, or creative/interactive ads. Below is a practical way to choose plus a short list of well-regarded vendors by strength.

What to consider when choosing a CTV agency
- Primary objective: brand reach, upper-funnel attention, mid-funnel retargeting, or direct-response/performance.  
- Inventory access: premium publisher deals (Roku, Hulu, linear TV networks) vs open-exchange programmatic buys.  
- Buying method & tech: DSP / programmatic expertise (The Trade Desk, Google DV360) vs direct-sold/guaranteed buys.  
- Measurement & attribution: use of third-party verification (Nielsen, Comscore), incremental lift testing, deterministic/identity solutions.  
- Creative capability: dynamic creative, A/B testing, interactive CTV formats, creative production optimized for living-room screens.  
- Transparency & reporting: impression-level logs, fee structure, viewability/frequency reporting.  
- Data & targeting: first-/second-party data onboarding, household targeting, cross-device linking.  
- Compliance & privacy: adherence to CCPA/GDPR and ID solutions you’re comfortable with.  
- Case studies & references in your vertical.

Categories and notable agencies/platforms
- Large/global, full-service (cross-screen strategy + scale): GroupM (WPP), Omnicom Media Group (OMD/PHD), Publicis Media, Dentsu. Good for big-brand, cross-channel campaigns and buying scale.  
- Programmatic DSPs / performance CTV (often used by agencies): The Trade Desk (platform), Amobee, Xandr/Microsoft Advertising (where available). These power many programmatic buys.  
- CTV-specialist platforms & measurement: Innovid (creative + measurement), VideoAmp (cross-platform measurement & optimization), Tremor Video (programmatic video), FreeWheel (premium publisher monetization).  
- SSPs / supply & publisher access: Magnite (including formerly SpotX), PubMatic — important if inventory quality matters.  
- Performance / DTC-focused agencies: Tinuiti, Merkle (for data-driven performance across channels), some independent growth shops often excel at direct-response CTV.  
- Creative-/experience-focused shops: VaynerMedia, R/GA, big creative agencies with CTV capabilities for storytelling and bespoke formats.  
- Boutique CTV specialists: many regionally focused boutiques can be excellent for mid-market advertisers — useful if you need hands-on customization and direct relationships.

Questions to ask shortlisted agencies
- Can you show recent CTV case studies with KPIs and verifiable measurement?  
- What inventory sources will you use (publisher/direct vs open exchange)? Can we review sample publishers?  
- Which DSPs/SSPs and verification vendors do you use? Do you give impression-level data?  
- How do you measure reach, frequency, viewability, and incremental lift?  
- What creative formats and personalization options do you offer? Can you do dynamic creative optimization?  
- How are fees structured (media markup, tech fees, access to data)?  
- What targeting options and data onboarding capabilities do you have?  
- Can you run a pilot test and what would success look like?

Quick next step
If you tell me your objective (brand vs performance), target region, monthly budget, and any existing tech stack (e.g., using The Trade Desk, DV360, Roku), I’ll recommend 3–5 agencies/platforms that best match your needs and a shortlist RFP template you can use.
